findings.title: PR proof comments repeat on every run
findings.description: `prBody` and `comment` redact posted proofs, but `publishPlan` still compares their GitHub text against the unredacted first line in `s.proofs`. If the machine's username is `runner`, redaction changes the fixed proof header, so each subsequent publication updates the PR body and reposts every proof comment after the first.

evidence.explanation: The fixed proof header contains the whole word `runner`; `publicText` replaces it when that is the username. `publishPlan` checks raw headers against the sanitized PR body and comment bodies, making both presence checks fail on each call.

findings.title: Short account names leak in comments
findings.description: `publicText` excludes home-path components and usernames shorter than three characters from its redaction list. On an account such as `/home/al`, a comment containing `user al` or a partial path containing `/home/al` retains that name when the full home path is absent.

evidence.explanation: The exact-home replacement only handles the complete path; the subsequent filter drops short components and the username before the regex can redact them. The comment wrapper posts the resulting text to GitHub.

location.code_snippet: +  const parts = [...new Set([...home.split('/').filter((p) => p && p !== 'home'), user].filter((p) => p && p.length >= 3))];
